pricing.freeTierCaps: 2 separate-track download hours total, 720p watermarked output and 44.1 kHz audio; single-track recording is unlimited
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; 14-day trial on paid plans
pricing.hiddenCosts: AI features consume credits and require top-ups after the included balance; higher registrant, studio and recording-volume needs push users to Business.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Riverside, assemble locally recorded guest tracks and produce a polished remote interview after the files exist. The hard boundary is browser recording reliability, isolated uploads, backups, live studio, and global media infrastructure, plus audio infrastructure, distribution, and production polish.
coreLoopDIY: Import locally recorded guest tracks, perform practical cleanup, assemble a polished remote interview episode, and export production files plus show notes.
whatYouLose: browser recording reliability, isolated uploads, backups, live studio, and global media infrastructure
moatNotes: audio infrastructure, distribution, and production polish
ongoingBurden: codec support, loudness standards, transcription, storage, feeds, analytics, and deliverability to directories
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Riverside because creators pay to remove fragile audio plumbing and publishing chores from a release schedule. The recurring cost buys codec support, loudness standards, transcription, storage, feeds, analytics, and deliverability to directories, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Audacity
priorArt.desc: Long-running open-source multitrack audio editor and useful implementation prior art.

alternatives.name: Kdenlive
alternatives.desc: A full video editor for locally recorded tracks; sync and polish are manual, but real.

facts.install: Install the official Windows, macOS or Linux package.
facts.engines: Speech-to-text can run local VOSK or OpenAI Whisper models.
facts.dataFormat: .kdenlive project files are MLT/XML references to local media; proxies, thumbnails and backups live in project folders.
facts.gapVsPaid: Kdenlive cannot capture remote guests or automatically recover and align their locally recorded tracks, so sync and cleanup are manual.
facts.setupBlocker: Core editing installs cleanly; local captioning requires downloading and configuring a speech model.

alternatives.name: Shotcut
alternatives.desc: A local interview editor with captions and noise tools; none of the remote-recording magic survives.

facts.install: Install an official Windows, macOS or Linux build; portable builds are also offered.
facts.engines: Speech-to-text runs local Whisper through whisper.cpp with downloadable GGML models.
facts.dataFormat: .mlt project files are MLT XML references to local media, with rendered files written wherever the user chooses.
facts.gapVsPaid: Shotcut edits existing files but provides none of Riverside's remote capture, guest upload recovery or automatic multitrack assembly.
facts.setupBlocker: Core editing installs cleanly; speech-to-text requires downloading a compatible Whisper model.

alternatives.name: Audacity
alternatives.desc: A multitrack editor for the files you already have; remote capture remains somebody else’s problem.

facts.install: Install the official Windows, macOS or Linux package.
facts.engines: Optional local Intel OpenVINO plugins add Whisper-based transcription and other AI audio effects.
facts.dataFormat: Audacity projects are local .aup3 SQLite databases; audio exports to standard formats, with optional Audio.com sharing.
facts.gapVsPaid: Audacity is audio-only and cannot replace Riverside's remote video capture or polished multicamera interview output.
facts.setupBlocker: Core editing installs cleanly; AI plugins are a separate, platform-dependent installation.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Standard plan and a single-creator production tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Riverside in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, ffmpeg, SQLite, and an HTMX interface; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: import locally recorded guest tracks, perform practical cleanup, assemble a polished remote interview episode, and export production files plus show notes.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create an upload queue and preserve originals in a read-only media folder.
Generate waveforms and non-destructive edit markers instead of rewriting source files.
Implement silence trimming, loudness normalization to -16 LUFS, fades, and noise-gate presets.
Add chapter markers, intro and outro slots, and a simple two-track timeline.
Produce a transcript and draft title, description, chapters, and social excerpts.
Export MP3, WAV, transcript, chapters JSON, and a complete project manifest.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out real-time remote recording.
Deliberately leave out podcast hosting and directory analytics.
Deliberately leave out licensed stock music and voice cloning.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
